pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood and agreed with no questions — asked 'any questions on training and mobility?' he answered 'No.' He had arrived already sold on the format and said so later: 'that was my whole reasoning for setting up this call to begin with. I wanted something convenient that I could make sure that I get done because it's in my garage.' He also engaged the recovery framing against his own pattern, agreeing 'I'm either all or nothing... When I go hard, I go all the way. And when I stop, I go all the way down.'

'No questions.' He mapped the framing straight onto his own experience — supplied the 80-20 label himself before the rep got there, and confirmed the eating window is already natural to him: 'I used to intermittent fast. When I did 75 hard, I did it. I was doing a 16 hour fast... I'm usually not a breakfast guy.' No resistance and no curiosity.

The only pillar he responded to in his own words rather than with a 'no questions': 'Listen, it seems catered, you know what I'm saying, where it's flexible to an extent. So that's important, especially when there's a lot of things, moving parts going around outside of fitness and health... Which is exactly what I'm looking for.' He tied it directly to the failure he had described — the 75 Hard result that did not survive contact with his real life.

anchors.raw: I was spending like $1,500 a month on training, but I had one-on-one training with a functional training facility where they worked only one-on-one, all the, what's it called, the Panthers and the hockey team around here and whatnot, they all trained there in the off-season.
anchors.competitor: Boutique functional training facility, South Florida
anchors.note: Recorded as undercuts_price because that is how it functioned on the call — the prospect used it to argue he would be paying 'plus or minus that same amount of money' for less service. The arithmetic says the opposite: $1,500 a month over the six-month programme is $9,000 against $6,000, so his own anchor supports the price by a third. The rep never ran the numbers. This is the highest-value unforced error in the batch.

anchors.raw: to have in-person training is not cheap. We're talking about $100 to $150 a session, but it's the same money, you know what I'm saying?
anchors.competitor: In-person personal training, general market rate
anchors.note: The per-session rate he quotes also undercuts his own argument — at three to four sessions a week for six months this is far above $6,000. He asserts 'it's the same money' twice and is not contradicted either time.

anchors.raw: I did 75 hard, and I went from 284 to 223.
anchors.note: A free protocol that delivered a 61 lb loss in 75 days. He has personal proof he can produce a dramatic result at zero cost, which is the strongest latent argument against paying anything. He also supplied the counter himself — it wrecked him with inflammation and he rebounded to 260 — and the rep used that to sell sustainability, which was the right instinct, but never named the free-alternative anchor directly.

anchors.raw: I'm in the construction world where I don't, I leave 10% hanging on every contract until I get completion at the very end.
anchors.note: A structural bias against paying up front, imported from his own industry and framed as professional discipline rather than doubt. It produced an immediate 50/50 interest-free concession from the rep. Worth watching for at scale: contractors and developers will bring this anchor to every call.

unmet_demand.want: In-person, hands-on coaching with a coach he can 'physically go touch something' with, plus access to facility equipment he does not own
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is remote by design — app, video review and text. The rep reframed around expertise scarcity, time saved and the single-kettlebell equipment requirement, all fair, but none of it delivers the thing asked for. This is a genuine boundary of the product, not a communication failure.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that loaded kettlebell work is safe with two bulging lumbar discs and bilateral shoulder impingement, given that his last return to training under load caused the shoulder injury
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted that Trevor 'will address all your pain areas' and that mobility protocols would reduce pain, then presented a guarantee of adding 8kg to his core kettlebell movements. Nobody asked what a clinician has said, whether overhead work is contraindicated, or what the programme does with a disc bulge. The prospect had explicitly flagged that overhead and chest pressing are the movements that break him.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that communication will not go quiet once payment clears — the reason he retains 10% on construction contracts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with a payment concession rather than with evidence. No response times were quoted, no service standard described, no client example given. The concern is about delivery and it was met with terms.
